chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umeyr, from Yahya ibn Musa Al-San'ani, who said:
I entered upon Abu Al-Hasan Al-Reza (peace be upon him) at Mina, and Abu Ja'far (the second, i.e., the third Imam) was upon his thigh, and he was peeling a banana for him and feeding him.

key_terms.أَبُو الْحَسَنِ الرِّضَا: Abu Al-Hasan Al-Reza, referring to Imam Ali ibn Musa (AS)
key_terms.أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ الثَّانِي: Abu Ja'far the second, referring to Imam Muhammad ibn Ali (AS), the third Imam
key_terms.مِنْى: Mina, a location near Mecca significant for Hajj rituals

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the Imam feeding his father a banana in Mina?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the humility and familial warmth of Imam Ali al-Rida (AS) by depicting him serving his father, Imam Muhammad al-Jawad (AS), a banana in Mina. It underscores the virtue of *birr al-walidayn* (kindness to parents) within the Imams' own household, serving as a practical model for Shia believers. The specific mention of the banana also connects to the chapter's focus on the Prophet's dietary recommendations and the physical and spiritual benefits of this fruit.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from his father, from Muhammad Bin Abu Umeyr, from Yahya Bin Musa Al Sanainy who said,

‘I went to Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> at Mina, and Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> the 2<sup>nd</sup> at Mina, and Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> the 3<sup>rd</sup> (9th Imam<sup>asws</sup>) was upon his<sup>asws</sup> thigh, and he<sup>asws</sup> was peeling a banana him<sup>asws</sup> and feeding him<sup>asws</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from his father from Muhammad ibn abu ‘Umayr from Yahya ibn Musa, San’aniy who has said the following: “
I once visited abu al-Hassan, al-Rida’, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, in Mina and abu Ja‘far, al-Thaniy was in his lap. He (the Imam) peeled banana and fed him (abu Ja‘far, al-Thaniy).”’
